==Description==
'''Mason Arch''' is a dawn [[Maps|map]] that takes place on masonry viaducts with a steel bridge connecting two ends of the viaduct.

'''Mason Arch''' has the [[All Paths]] modifier, which duplicates most enemies that spawn. It increases all currency rewards by 10%.

==Design & Paths==
'''Mason Arch''' consists of two parallel railway tracks on a brick viaduct. The railway is situated in a hilly valley with trees, and crosses a river. Near the entrance of the tunnels, there are twin bore tunnels into the side of a hill. Right after the tunnels, there are maintenance bridges that span the gap between the parallel viaducts. Several emergency waiting points can be seen in between the gaps of the viaducts.
Immediately after the tunnel, there are two station platforms, with a train indicator and abandoned shelves to place cliff towers on. This elevated station platforms are connected to the ground by a spiral staircase. The railway then crosses the bridge on a rusted steel bridge, with two light rail trains running on the bridge, where cliff towers can be placed upon. After, the viaduct briefly continues before entering another twin bore tunnel.

The two paths starts and ends at the twin bore tunnel. The paths are fairly straight, save for the crossing of one of the maintenance bridges and the crossing of the paths on the steel bridge.

==Rewards==
The game calculates how many {{Coins|Coins}} and {{Exp|}} you receive based on how many waves you survived and if you won a match. During periods of 50% more {{Exp|}} (Friday – Sunday), any {{Exp|}} earned is multiplied by 1.5x through the [[XP Boost]] modifier. The VIP [[Gamepasses|gamepass]] also multiplies any {{Exp|}} earned by 1.25x through the [[VIP Boost]] modifier. These two boosts are additive. Regular {{Exp|}} boosts are multiplicative with other modifiers present on this map.

Any rewards that end in a decimal point is rounded down, no matter the first figure of the leading decimal.

{{Rewards|Insane|Modifiers = 1.1|Hardcore = Hide|Voidcore = Hide}}

==Strategy==
*All enemies, except the major boss spawn twice on this map due to the [[All Paths]] modifier.
**Because of this, you may want to consider using towers that can do AOE damage, such as the [[Mortar]].
***The [[Rocketeer]] should not be used as has a dead zone range, whilst the ground space is quite limited.
**The increased amount of enemies allows you to gain more cash by damaging enemies.
***The [[Cowboy]] and [[Golden Cowboy]] can also generate more cash because of this.
*There are multiple intersections where both paths cross. It is recommended to place your towers at the intersections near the entrances or the intersection near the trains.
**The [[Assassin]] excels at this spot. Its pierce may be helpful to clear out the hordes of enemies caused by the [[All Paths]] modifier.
*Cliff space is quite limited towards the start of this map, therefore bringing cliff towers may not be a great option.
**The trains in the central portion of the map can be where most of your cliff towers can be placed, and they will be in a great spot to be boosted by support towers, like the [[Commander]].

==Trivia==
*'''Mason Arch''' was named after [[wp:Marble_Arch_tube_station|Marble Arch tube station]] in London.
**However, that tube station is situated underground, while this map is entirely based above ground.
**The setting is based on a combination of the [[wp:Welland Viaduct|Welland Viaduct]] on the [[wp:Oakham–Kettering line|Oakham–Kettering line]] in East Midlands, England, and [[wp:Monkwearmouth Railway Bridge|Monkwearmouth Railway Bridge]] in Wearside, England.
**The elevated platforms are based on [[wp:Mill Hill East_tube_station|Mill Hill East tube station]] in London.
***Incidentally, this arrangement of platforms is similar to [[wp:St Peter's Metro station|St Peter's Metro station]] in Sunderland, England, the station before the [[wp:Monkwearmouth Railway Bridge|Monkwearmouth Railway Bridge]].
****The system that calls at this station, the [[wp:Tyne and Wear Metro|Tyne and Wear Metro]], is also a light rail system, the same as the railway system that this map depicts.
*The two trains that are seen on this map are based on [[wp:Docklands Light Railway rolling stock|Docklands Light Railway B07 stock]].
**Furthermore, the turquoise roundel that is used for the [[wp:Docklands Light Railway|Docklands Light Railway]] can be seen on the platforms of this map.
*At the bottom of the elevated platforms, a [[wp:British Rail Double Arrow|British Rail Double Arrow]] sign can be seen, indicating that the station name is ''Southgate''.
**This is based on [[wp:Southgate_tube_station|Southgate tube station]] in London, though National Rail trains do not run here in real life.
**It is also named after the former England football team manager, [[wp:Gareth Southgate|Gareth Southgate]].
*On one of the spiral staircases, three trophies can be seen.
**These are the {{RLinkC|9929824308|UEFA Champions League Trophy}}, {{RLinkC|10484655503|UEFA Super Cup Trophy}} and the {{RLinkC|10928926554|Euros Trophy (Women's)}} in the Roblox catalog.
*'''Mason Arch''' used to appear in the special [[Elevators]], though this is no longer the case due to them being removed from the game.
**It appeared in both regular and special [[Elevators]].
**As '''Mason Arch''' never received its own [[Matchmaking]] statue like other special maps and is quite similar to other maps that were not considered special, like the [[Black Spot Exchange]], it is no longer considered a special map.
*The previous incarnation of this map is called [https://www.roblox.com/games/3581407761/TDS-Map-Viaduct Viaduct].
